observation.visible_scene: An outdoor close-up of a small fire burning on a flat tan cardboard sheet laid over dry, brownish grass. A pile of crumpled, blackened paper/cardboard sits at the center of the sheet, actively flaming with bright orange-yellow tongues of fire. A large, out-of-focus beige vertical object (a wall or container edge) occludes the left side of the frame throughout. The fire remains anchored to the same charred pile for the whole excerpt.
visible_changes: The flames continuously flicker, rise, collapse and reshape from frame to frame, with the brightest core shifting position over the pile while the overall fire footprint stays roughly the same size.
Around t≈1.0–1.03 s a small detached burning fragment/ember lifts briefly above the upper-left of the flames before the fire pattern settles again.

The framing drifts slowly (handheld camera motion): the blurry left foreground object slides leftward and a small printed cardboard box/label with markings becomes progressively visible at the left edge of the burning sheet, while the grass background shifts rightward; this is camera movement, not motion of the fire or the sheet.
The charred pile itself does not translate; only its flame envelope and the exposed unburned edges of paper change shape.
outside_clip_unknowns: What ignited the pile and any earlier burning stage before t=0.
Whether the fire grows, sustains, or dies out after t=1.33 s.
The exact identity of the blurry foreground object and the surface the cardboard rests on.
uncertain_details: Direction and type of camera motion (pan vs. lateral drift) is inferred only from relative shifts of foreground and background and is not fully determined.
Whether the lifted orange speck is a separate ember or just a flame tongue.
Material composition of the burning pile (paper vs. cardboard) cannot be confirmed visually.
Overall fire intensity trend (steady vs. increasing) is not clearly established over this short window.
